title: introduce-credential-cascade-and-slim-iterator-pullstream-for-go-sdk
author: Diego Alvarez
release_notes: Go SDK v1.6.2: credential fallback chain, slimmer PullStream iterator, per-stream retry window config, minor ergonomics and docs updates.
body:
Summary: This PR introduces a compact credential cascade (credential fallback chain) for the Go SDK and refactors the PullStream iterator into a slimmer, ergonomics-focused iterator surface. The goal is parity with newer TS/Python ergonomics while keeping the Go footprint small and allocation-friendly.

Motivation: Customers reported friction when their token provider rotated unexpectedly during long-lived streaming sessions; we observed repeated token refresh retries and duplicated reconnect attempts. At the same time, the current PullStream iterator surface in go-sdk had a few ergonomic rough edges (blocking Read semantics, inconsistent context propagation, and heavy per-chunk allocations) compared to TS/Python counterparts.

Changes: - Add credential cascade: an ordered chain of credential providers (env -> file -> delegated provider -> runtime refresh hook). The cascade is pluggable and preserves existing default behavior but makes it trivial to add a short-circuit fallback provider for dedicated/private deployments. - Introduce CredentialProvider interface with GetToken(ctx) and optional Prewarm(ctx) hooks. - Implement DelegatedProvider shim used by redwood Private customers that need short-lived delegated tokens; the shim includes jittered warmup and transparent refresh. - Slim PullIterator: replaced old PullStream.ReadRaw with PullIterator.Next(ctx) returning a typed Result and an Error sentinel. The iterator is non-blocking-friendly and reduces allocations by reusing a small buffer pool for streaming chunk assembly. - Per-stream retry window: expose a StreamRetryWindow config that constrains automatic reauth/retry attempts for individual stream sessions (useful for low-latency flows that prefer fast failover to fallback models). - Session pinning opt: a small API to pin a stream to a session lease when callers want session-affinity across reconnects. - Backwards-compat: adapter shim for old ReadRaw callers included; deprecation notice added to comments. - Tests: end-to-end integration harness added that simulates token expiry mid-stream and verifies single reconnect and resume.

Commits (high-level): - 8d21c4f: introduce credential cascade types and default chain - b3f2a90: add DelegatedProvider shim and warmup logic - c7a7d85: refactor PullStream into PullIterator with buffer pool - 4f9e303: add StreamRetryWindow and session pinning API - 91a4b55: add integration test harness and CI job - 2b7c1d2: docs and examples, deprecation adapters, changelog

Files changed (high level): - internal/auth/credential_cascade.go (new) - internal/auth/delegated_provider.go (new) - public/cred_provider.go (new interface + docs) - public/stream/iterator.go (refactor: new PullIterator) - public/stream/adapter_compat.go (adapter for ReadRaw) - examples/streaming/cred_fallback_example.go (new) - tests/integration/stream_token_rotate_test.go (new) - docs/sdk-go/streaming.md (updates) - ci/jobs/stream-integration.yaml (adds new job)

Design notes: - The credential cascade is intentionally minimal: providers return a token and TTL; the cascade respects TTL and defers to a fast-path provider when tokens are fresh. - DelegatedProvider implements an exponential jittered Prewarm to avoid thundering herd during churn. - PullIterator.Next(ctx) returns (Result, bool) style internally but surface returns a small struct with EventType/Bytes/Meta to make downstream switch handling obvious. - Reuse of a sync.Pool for chunk buffers cut allocations in local benchmarks by ~35% for 8k average chunk size.

Backwards compatibility: - The adapter_compat preserves old ReadRaw semantics by delegating to the new iterator; it logs a single-level deprecation warning and will be removed in a future major version.

Testing & CI: - New integration job (ci/jobs/stream-integration.yaml) runs against a local test harness that can inject token expiry and network stalls. - Unit tests for credential cascade, DelegatedProvider, and iterator behavior. - CI initially flaked on a timing-sensitive integration test (first run failed due to race in test harness); I bumped a test timeout and added deterministic jitter control. Subsequent runs passed.

Performance: - Microbenchmarks included: iterator allocation profile, buffer reuse, and token-provider latency. - On a small benchmark (simulated 100 concurrent streams, 8k chunks), median p90 CPU went down ~9% and total GC pause decreased.

Migration notes: - Consumers using the older PullStream.ReadRaw API should either migrate to PullIterator.Next or keep using the adapter shim. - If you rely on custom credential providers, implement the CredentialProvider interface and register it in the SDK's Chain. - The default chain is unchanged; opt-in required to enable DelegatedProvider.

Security considerations: - DelegatedProvider is opt-in and requires callers to supply a trusted short-lived token endpoint. - Token values are held only in memory and never logged.

Review conversation: - Claire Thompson (2026-02-13): "Nice cleanup — can we make the Prewarm backoff configurable via a small struct so Private deployments can tune aggressively? Also, please add an example showing DelegatedProvider error handling." - Diego Alvarez reply (2026-02-13): "Good call — added PrewarmConfig and example in examples/streaming/cred_fallback_example.go. DelegatedProvider already returns typed errors; updated docs with usage pattern." - Ethan Liu (2026-02-14): "Iterator looks good; one nit on naming: Next returns StreamEvent vs Result — prefer StreamEvent for clarity." - Diego Alvarez reply (2026-02-14): "Renamed Result -> StreamEvent in public surface and adjusted adapters; updated tests." - Maya Patel (2026-02-15): "Integration test flaky on first run; we should ensure deterministic jitter in CI. Also, add a small comment about buffer pool sizing." - Diego Alvarez reply (2026-02-15): "Added deterministic jitter flag in CI harness and documented pool sizing heuristics in streaming.md." - Claire Thompson approval (2026-02-16): "LGTM after small nit fixes addressed."

CI summary: - Unit: pass - Integration (stream-integration): pass (after one rerun) - Lint: pass - Vet/govet: pass

Merge outcome: Squash and merge to main.

Post-merge followups: - ENG-3498: add a telemetry metric for 'credential_fallback_used' to Console dashboards (tracked). - ENG-3520: propose a TS/Python parity doc to ensure DelegatedProvider behavior matches across SDKs.

Notes for release: This is a minor release bump: v1.6.2. No breaking changes; old APIs remain supported via shim. Changelog entry updated in docs/changelog.md.

Checklist: - [x] Tests added (unit + integration) - [x] Docs updated - [x] Backwards-compat adapter included - [x] Benchmarks and perf notes included - [x] Reviewer approvals obtained

This PR is intentionally focused on ergonomics and reliability for long-lived streams; it should reduce reconnection churn caused by credential rotation and improve SDK ergonomics for Go consumers while aligning behavior with TS/Python SDKs.
